content_voiceover: This classic association question pairs specific mutations with their myeloid neoplasm entities. CSF3R mutations are strongly linked to chronic neutrophilic leukemia, that pairing is correct. PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1 rearrangements, and PCM1-JAK2 fusions are the defining lesions of myeloid or lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia, also correct, and importantly these entities, apart from PCM1-JAK2 to some extent, are exquisitely imatinib sensitive. KIT D816V is the hallmark mutation of systemic mastocytosis, correct as well, and JAK2 V617F is essentially synonymous with polycythemia vera, found in the vast majority of cases. The wrong pairing is option E. SETBP1 mutations are actually characteristic of atypical CML and CMML, not MDS/MPN with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis, which is instead defined by its high rate of SF3B1 mutations often co-occurring with JAK2 V617F. Mixing up SETBP1 with the wrong overlap syndrome is exactly the kind of gene-disease mismatch these questions test.
keypoints: CSF3R mutation strongly associated with chronic neutrophilic leukemia
PDGFRA/B, FGFR1, PCM1-JAK2 define myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia
KIT D816V hallmark of systemic mastocytosis; JAK2 V617F hallmark of PV
SETBP1 belongs to aCML/CMML, not MDS/MPN-RS-T (which is SF3B1 driven)
keypoint_voiceover: Lock in these gene-disease pairs, CSF3R with chronic neutrophilic leukemia, PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, and PCM1-JAK2 with eosinophilic myeloid neoplasms, KIT D816V with systemic mastocytosis, and JAK2 V617F with polycythemia vera. SETBP1 belongs to atypical CML and CMML, not to MDS/MPN with ring sideroblasts and thrombocytosis, which is really an SF3B1 story.
